rows.abstract: "Magna Carta for Senior Citizens" Applies to all elderly resident citizens of the Philippines, aged 60 years and above. Provides penalty for violation of this Act.

rows.author: A046
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE NATIONAL COUNCIL FOR THE WELFARE OF SENIOR CITIZENS (NCWSC) AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Defines the objectives of the proposed Council, namely: (1) To prepare and adopt an integrated and comprehensive long-term National Geriatic and Rehabilitation Plan to ensure the protection of the rights of the senior citizens and provide them adequate health, geriatic, rehabilitative and socio-economic care and services; (2) To propose new policies and new legislation, or amendments to existing ones, that will ensure the attainment of its objectives; (3) To act as an over-all coordinating body, to rationalize the functions and activities of government agencies, nongovernment organizations, private entities and international organizations oeprating in the Philippines, and the affecting the senior citizens; (4) To ensure the fullest particiipation and involvement of senior citizens in the geriatic and rehabilitation process; and (5) To educate and re-orient the general public in its attitude and thinking towards senior citizens.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 1997-06-03

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSURING DUE PROCESS AND PREVENTING ABUSE IN THE ISSUANCE AND IMPLEMENTATION OF HOLD-DEPARTURE ORDERS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR ANY VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: Rationale: The right to travel is guaranteed by the Constitution and the United Nations Universal Declaration of Human Rights to which the Philippines is a signatory.> The Constitution, however, does not indicate the person who has the power to determine when the right can be curtailed "in the interest of national security, public safety, or public health." Thus, the power is open to abuse by adminsitrative or nonjudicial officers who may imprudently exercise it at the "inconvenience and annoyance" of those who desire to exercise their constitutional right to travel. Provides for these concerns: (1) The proper trial court; (2) Action on the petition for a hold-departure order; (3) Evidence of guilt;l (4) Proper court order; and (5) Penaltyy for violation of this process.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1997-06-04

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING PRIVATE EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS FROM CERTAIN TAXES AND DUTIES
rows.abstract: Rationale: To a large extent, the private educational institutions have assumed an indispensable role in molding the minds and character of the youth in order to prepare them for social, civic and political responsibilitie s. In recognition of theirunique role,  the Constitution upholds the importance of the private educational institutions in nation building as a collaborative partner of the State by enabling Congress with the power to legislate measures that will grant them incentives. Applies to all persons  or entities engaged in any of the activities  of an educational institution , whether organized for profit or not.> Proposes that said institution be EXEMPT from the following taxes: (1) income tax; (2) tax on transfer of property;; (3) VAT and  other percentage taxes; (4) documentary stamp tax; (5) real property taxes; (6) capital gains tax; (7) gross receipt taxes; and (8) taxes on interest from bank deposits.

rows.abstract: Rationale: Nothing is more pathetic than to see sick men, women and children, especially the underprivileged , being deprived of the necessary health care due to the lack of health care facilities and absence of funds.  In order to alleviate these pressing problems, the proposed bill seeks to provide hospitals with a direct source of funds and to increase their savings to expand operations that deal directly with health care. > Declares that siand institution be EXEMPT from these taxes: Incomereal property; VAT; documtanry stamp; capital gains; tax on interest from bank deposits. >Provides, likewise, for their exemption from payment of customs duties.

rows.abstract: Covers all natural-born Filipinos who have subsequently acquired other citizenship by reason of marriage or domicile abroad. These rights include: (1) the right to practice one's profession even if the degree is earned abroad; provided, they passedthe requirements set by the proper government regulating body, which requirements shall not include the qualification of Filipino citizenship; (2) the right to acquire properties, real or personal; (3) the right of suffrage; (4) the right to tax exemption benefits granted by law to Filipino citizens;  (5) the right to invest even in areas of business limited to Filipino citizens; and (6) the right to explore and enjoy natural resources limited to Filipino citizens.

rows.title_full: AN ACT RECLASSIFYING THE SYSTEM OF IRRIGATION FACILITIES OF THE NATIONAL IRRIGATION ADMINISTRATION AS INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECT; AND IN THE PROCESS ABSOLVING OUTSTANDING LOANS EXTENDED BY THE NATIONAL IRRIGATION ADMINISTRATION TO RICE FARMERS, BE IT INDIVIDUALS, ASSOCIATIONS, OR COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS
rows.abstract: Provides for the following --- "SECTION 1. The loans facility extended by the National Irrigation Administration to rice farmers for the operation of irrigation facilities, whether granted to individuals or groups through irrigator's associations orcommunity-based organizations shall be considered as infrastructure investment of the State similar to roads, bridges and the like." "SECTION 2. The use of irrigation facilities through the National Irrigation Administration shall therefore be freeof charge for maintenance, which the State has amply and regularly supported on annual appropriations. " "SECTION 3. The National Irrigation Adminsitration is mandated to update all its pertinent records prior to the implementation of this Act and coonsequently write-off the outstanding obligations of the farmers, principal and any interest accruing thereto, from its books of account."

The banks of rivers and streams and the shores of the seas and lakes throughout their enture length and within the zone to be determined by the Council en banc and updated by the same every other five (5) years, shall be subject to the easement of public use in the interest of recreation, navigation, flotage, fishing, salvage and preservation of these areas for the sustainable use of such rivers, streams seas andlakes. rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR SCHOLARSHIPS AND OTHER BENEFITS FOR PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SCHOOLTEACHERS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: It is quite disappointing to read reports of the Commission on Higher Education that more than half of the 500,000 instructors and professors in 1,269 public and private colleges and universities nationwide are not academically qualifiedto teach.  This is so because they lack the minimum requirement of a masters degree in the arts or sciences. Moreso CHED contends that this was one of the main factors which contributed to the decline of the quality of education in higher learning institutions. Prescribes the criteria to qualify for said scholarship; covers graduate and post-gradaute courses. Provides, likewise, for educational benefits to the recipient's children, including a longevity pay for the teachers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 1997-07-29

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING RETIREMENT BENEFITS FOR ALL ELECTIVE AND APPOINTIVE BARANGAY OFFICIALS WHO HAVE RENDERED SEVEN CONSECUTIVE YEARS OF SERVICE IN THEIR BARANGAYS AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Since their level is the closest to the people, barangay officials are practically working on a 24 - hour shift, without rest even on holidays.  And this, they perform for a measly honoraria or allowance every month. Worse, they will notreceive any form of remuneration or benefits once they retire from office. Declares the following --- "SECTION 1. All elective and appointive barangay officials who have rendered at least seven (7) consecutive years of service in their respective barangays, are hereby entitled to receive for life, upon their retirement, a monthly pension equivalent to 75% of the total honorarium he received his incumbency." "SECTION 2. All incumbents to the positions above stated who have served for at least sevven (7) consecutive years before the May 1997 Barangay Elections and prior to the passage of this law shall be benefited by the retroactive effect of this act."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 1997-07-29
